entries.sanskrit: स कर्दमस् तं स्वेऽवस्थितं दृष्ट्वा मूर्ध्ना क्षिताव् अपतत् गीर्भिश् चाभ्यगृणाद् (१२) इति चतुर्णाम् अन्वयः । पद्मोत्पले दिन-रात्रि-विकासे । सितानां पद्मानाम् उत्पलानां च स्रक् यस्य तम् । स्निग्धा नीलाश् च येऽलकास् तेषां व्रातो वक्त्राब्जे यस्य ॥९॥

He wears a garland of white lotuses and water-lilies; a mass of soft, dark curls is on his lotus face.

entries.sanskrit:
त्वाम् ऋते परमानन्दं धिग् अन्य-वर-कामुकम् ।

अथापि कृपणं मानुगृहाण वर-दानतः ॥

बतेति हर्षे । हे ईड्य ! नोऽस्माभिः समग्र-सत्त्व-निधेस् तव दर्शनाद् अद्याक्ष्णोः सांसिद्ध्यं साफल्यं जुष्टं सेवितम् । त्वद्-दर्शनम् एव महा-फलम् इत्य् उपपादयति । यस्य तव दर्शनं सद्भिर् उत्तरोत्तरम् आपादित-प्रकर्षैर् जन्मभी रूढो विरूढो योगो यैस् तेऽपि ॥१३॥
word_for_word: tvām ṛte paramānandaṃ dhig anya-vara-kāmukam athāpi kṛpaṇaṃ mānugṛhāṇa vara-dānataḥ
“Without you, O supreme bliss, fie on the one who desires another boon! Yet, kindly grant a boon to this poor one”
bateti harṣe
“bata” expresses joy
he īḍya
“O praiseworthy one”
no’smābhiḥ samagra-sattva-nidhes tava darśanād adyākṣṇoḥ sāṃsiddhyaṃ sāphalyaṃ juṣṭaṃ sevitam
today, by seeing you, treasure of all existence, our eyes have attained fulfillment and success
tvad-darśanam eva mahā-phalam ity upapādayati
he establishes that seeing you is itself the great fruit
yasya tava darśanaṃ sadbhir uttarottaram āpādita-prakarṣair janmabhī rūḍho virūḍho yogo yais te’pi
even those whose yoga has grown through increasingly excellent births attained by the good [seek that vision]
entries.literal_english: “Without you, O supreme bliss, fie on the one who desires another boon! Yet, kindly grant a boon to this poor one.” “Bata” expresses joy. “O praiseworthy one!” Today, through seeing you, the treasure of all existence, our eyes have attained fulfillment and success. He establishes that seeing you is itself the great fruit: even those whose yoga has grown through increasingly excellent births, attained by the good, [find its fulfillment in seeing you].

entries.sanskrit: स-काम-भक्तान् विगर्हयन्न् आह---य इति । हे ईश ! ये निरयेऽपि स्युः, तेषां कामानां लवाय ये त्वन्-मायया नष्ट-बुद्धयः, त एवोपासते । त्वं तु तेषां तान् कामान् अपि रासि ददासि ॥१४॥
word_for_word: sa-kāma-bhaktān vigarhayann āha ya iti
he criticizes devotees who worship with desires, saying “yaḥ”
he īśa ye niraye’pi syuḥ teṣāṃ kāmānāṃ lavāya ye tvan-māyayā naṣṭa-buddhayaḥ ta evopāsate
“O Lord, those whose understanding is destroyed by Your māyā worship You for even a particle of the desires they would have in hell”
tvaṃ tu teṣāṃ tān kāmān api rāsi dadāsi
but You grant them those very desires
entries.literal_english: He criticizes devotees who worship with desires, saying “yaḥ.” “O Lord, those whose understanding has been destroyed by Your māyā worship You for even a particle of the desires they would have in hell. But You grant them those very desires.”

entries.sanskrit: यः स-कामान् निन्दामि, सोऽहम् अपि तादृश एवेत्य् आह---तथेति । गृह-मेधो गृहाश्रमस् तत्र धेनुं त्रि-वर्ग-दोग्ध्रीं भार्यां परिवोढु-कामः परिणेतुम् इच्छन् काम-दुघाङ्घ्रिपस्य कल्प-द्रुमस्य तव मूलम् अङ्घ्रिम् उपेयिवान् उपागतोऽस्मि । ननु कामाद्य्-अर्थम् अन्यत् किम् अप्य् उपास्यताम् ? न, यतोऽशेषस्य पुरुषार्थस्य मूलम् एतद् एव ॥१५॥
word_for_word: yaḥ sa-kāmān nindāmi so’ham api tādṛśa evety āha---tatheti
“I who criticize those with desires am myself just like that,” he says with “tathā”
gṛha-medho gṛhāśramas tatra
“gṛhamedha” means household life
dhenuṃ tri-varga-dogdhrīṃ bhāryāṃ parivoḍhu-kāmaḥ pariṇetum icchan
wishing to marry a wife who, like a cow, yields the three aims of life
kāma-dughāṅghripasya kalpa-drumasya tava mūlam aṅghrim upeyivān upāgato’smi
I have come to the root—Your feet—of the wish-fulfilling tree that grants every desire
nanu kāmādy-artham anyat kim apy upāsyatām
one might ask, “Why not worship something else for desires and the like?”
na yato’śeṣasya puruṣārthasya mūlam etad eva
no, because You alone are the root of every human aim
entries.literal_english: “I who criticize those with desires am myself just like that,” he says with “tathā.” “Gṛhamedha” means household life. Wishing to marry a wife who, like a cow, yields the three aims of life, I have come to the root—Your feet—of the wish-fulfilling tree that grants every desire. One might ask, “Why not worship something else for desires and the like?” No: You alone are the root of every human aim.

entries.sanskrit: ननु तर्हि मुक्त्य्-अर्थम् एव किं न भजसि अनधिकारात् ? इत्य् आह---हे अधीश ! यस् त्वं प्रजापतिः, तस्य तव वचसा तन्त्र्यायं काम-हतो लोकः पशुवद् बद्धः । हे शुक्ल ! शुद्ध-धर्म-मूर्ते ! अहं च किल लोकानुगतः, अतस् तुभ्यं बलिं वहामि, कर्म-मयीं त्वद्-आज्ञाम् अनुवर्ते । अनिमिषाय कालात्मने । तद्-अर्थं भार्यां चेच्छामीति च-कारस्यार्थः । न केवलं लोकानुगतो बलिं वहामि, किन्तु ऋण-त्रयापाकरणार्थम् इति किलेत्य् उक्तम् ॥१६॥
word_for_word: nanu tarhi mukty-artham eva kiṃ na bhajasi anadhikārāt ity āha
“Then why do you not worship solely for liberation?”—because you are not qualified, he says
he adhīśa yas tvaṃ prajāpatiḥ tasya tava vacasā tantryāyaṃ kāma-hato lokaḥ paśuvad baddhaḥ
“O Lord of lords, You are Prajāpati; by Your command this world, struck by desire, is bound like an animal”
he śukla śuddha-dharma-mūrte ahaṃ ca kila lokānugataḥ
“O Śukla, embodiment of pure dharma, I indeed follow the people”
atas tubhyaṃ baliṃ vahāmi karma-mayīṃ tvad-ājñām anuvarte
therefore I offer tribute to You and obey Your command, which takes the form of prescribed action
animiṣāya kālātmane
“for the Unblinking One,” the personification of time
tad-arthaṃ bhāryāṃ cecchāmīti ca-kārasyārthaḥ
“and” means that for this purpose I also desire a wife
na kevalaṃ lokānugato baliṃ vahāmi kintu ṛṇa-trayāpākaraṇārtham iti kilety uktam
“indeed” indicates that I offer tribute not only because I follow worldly custom but also to discharge the three debts
entries.literal_english: “Then why do you not worship solely for liberation?”—because you are not qualified, he says. “O Lord of lords, You are Prajāpati; by Your command this world, struck by desire, is bound like an animal. O Śukla, embodiment of pure dharma, I follow the people; therefore I offer tribute to You and obey Your command, which takes the form of prescribed action. ‘For the Unblinking One,’ the personification of time. ‘And’ means that for this purpose I also desire a wife. The word ‘indeed’ indicates that I offer tribute not only because I follow worldly custom but also to discharge the three debts.”

entries.sanskrit: अनिमिषायेत्य् अनेन कालात्मकात् त्वत्तो भीतः कर्म करोमीत्य् उक्तम् । एतत् तु भयं त्वद्-भक्तानां नास्तीत्य् आह द्वाभ्याम् । लोकान् कामाभिभूतांस् तान् अनुसृतान् पशूंश् च । विवेके सत्य् अपि पुनः कर्म-जडान् मादृशान् हित्वा अनादृत्य ये तव चरण-रूपम् आतपत्रं श्रिताः, तान् एवाह---त्वद्-गुणानां वादः कथा, तद् एव सीधु मदिरा, संसार-विस्मारकत्वात् । पीयूषं रुचि-करत्वात् । तेन निर्यापिता विलापिता देह-धर्माः क्षुत्-पिपासादयो यैः, एषाम् इत्य् उत्तरेणान्वयः ॥१७॥

entries.literal_english: By saying “for the Unblinking One,” he has said, “I act out of fear of You, who are time personified.” He says in two verses that this fear does not exist for Your devotees. The people overwhelmed by desire, their followers, and animals; even those who possess discernment but, like me, are dull in action—having abandoned them, those who have taken shelter of the umbrella that is Your feet are described. The discourse on Your qualities is a story; it is wine because it makes one forget worldly existence, and nectar because it is delightful. Those who have been made to cast off bodily conditions such as hunger and thirst by that [story] are the people referred to next.

entries.sanskrit: तव यत् त्रिणाभि काल-चक्रं, तज् जगद् आच्छिद्य आकृष्य धावद् अपि एषां त्वद्-भक्तानाम् आयुर् आच्छिद्य धावन् न भवति । कथं भूतम् ? अजरं ब्रह्म तस्मिन्न् अक्ष-रूपे भ्रमिर् भ्रमणम् । भ्रमद् इति वक्तव्येऽतिभ्रमण-शीलत्वाद् उपचारेण भ्रमिर् इत्य् अभेद-निर्देशः । अधिक-मासेन सह त्रयोदश मासा अरा यस्य । त्रि-शतं षष्टिश् चाहो-रात्राः पर्वाणि यस्य । शत-शब्दे विभक्तेर् अलुग् आर्षः । षड् ऋतवो नेमयो यस्य । अनन्ताः क्षण-लवादयश् छदाः पत्राणि पत्राकारा धाराः सन्ति यस्य । त्रीणि चातुर्मास्यानि नाभय आधार-भूतानि वलयानि यस्य । कराल-स्रोतस् तीव्र-वेगम् । एतैर् विशेषणैर् एव संवत्सरात्मकं चक्रम् उक्तम् इति द्रष्टव्यम् ॥१८॥
word_for_word: tava yat triṇābhi kāla-cakraṃ taj jagad ācchidya ākṛṣya dhāvad api
Your three-naved wheel of time, while running, cuts through and draws along the universe
eṣāṃ tvad-bhaktānām āyur ācchidya dhāvan na bhavati
it does not cut off the lifespan of these devotees
kathaṃ bhūtam ajaraṃ brahma tasminn akṣa-rūpe bhramir bhramaṇam
how is it constituted? Brahman is undecaying; the rotation is on its axle
bhramad iti vaktavye’ti-bhramaṇa-śīlatvād upacāreṇa bhramir ity abheda-nirdeśaḥ
although “revolving” might be expected, “rotation” is figuratively used to indicate exceptionally rapid circling
adhika-māsena saha trayodaśa māsā arā yasya
it has thirteen spokes, with the intercalary month
tri-śataṃ ṣaṣṭiś cāho-rātrāḥ parvāṇi yasya
its joints are the three hundred and sixty days and nights
śata-śabde vibhakter alug ārṣaḥ
the case ending after the word “hundred” is retained in the archaic form
ṣaḍ ṛtavo nemayo yasya
its rims are the six seasons
anantāḥ kṣaṇa-lavādayaś chadāḥ patrāṇi patrākārā dhārāḥ santi yasya
its leaves, or leaf-shaped blades, are the endless moments and instants
trīṇi cātur-māsyāni nābhaya ādhāra-bhūtāni valayāni yasya
its three hubs are the supporting circles of the three four-month seasons
karāla-srotas tīvra-vegam
it has a terrible, swift current
etair viśeṣaṇair eva saṃvatsarātmakaṃ cakram uktam iti draṣṭavyam
these descriptions are to be understood as specifying the wheel that is the year
entries.literal_english: Your three-naved wheel of time, while running, cuts through and draws along the universe, but it does not cut off the lifespan of these devotees. How is it constituted? Brahman is undecaying; the rotation is on its axle. “Bhrami” is used figuratively for “revolving,” by an identity of expression that conveys exceptionally rapid rotation. It has thirteen spokes, with the intercalary month; its joints are the three hundred and sixty days and nights; its rims are the six seasons; its leaves, or leaf-shaped blades, are the endless moments and instants; its three hubs are the supporting circles of the three four-month seasons. It has a terrible, swift current. These descriptions are to be understood as specifying the wheel that is the year.

entries.sanskrit: ननु निरुपाधिम् उदासीनं मां किं याचसे ? तथापि मायया विश्व-सृष्ट्य्-आदि-कर्तृत्वात् त्वम् एव याच्यः । इत्य् आह---स्वयम् एक एव सन्न् अप्य् आत्मन्य् अधिकृतया योग-मायया हेतु-भूतया याः स्वी-कृताः शक्तयः सत्त्वाद्याः, ताभिः । अदो विश्वम् । स्व-व्यतिरिक्त-साधनानपेक्षत्वे दृष्टान्तः---यथेति ॥१९॥
word_for_word: nanu nirupādhim udāsīnaṃ māṃ kiṃ yācase
“Why do you ask me, who am without limiting adjuncts and detached?”
tathāpi māyayā viśva-sṛṣṭy-ādi-kartṛtvāt tvam eva yācyaḥ
even so, since by māyā You perform the creation of the universe and the rest, You alone are to be asked
ity āha---svayam eka eva sann apy ātmany adhikṛtayā yoga-māyayā hetu-bhūtayā
he says: although You alone exist, through yogamāyā acting within You as the cause
yāḥ svī-kṛtāḥ śaktayaḥ sattvādyāḥ tābhiḥ
by the powers such as sattva which You have assumed
ado viśvam
this universe
sva-vyatirikta-sādhanānapekṣatve dṛṣṭāntaḥ---yatheti
“as” gives an example of not needing an instrument separate from oneself
entries.literal_english: “Why do you ask me, who am without limiting adjuncts and detached?” Even so, since by māyā You perform the creation of the universe and the rest, You alone are to be asked. He says: although You alone exist, the powers such as sattva, which You have assumed within Yourself through yogamāyā acting as their cause, bring about this universe. “As” gives an example of not needing an instrument separate from oneself.

entries.sanskrit: यद्य् अपि मायिकत्वाद् भक्तेभ्यो विषय-सुखं दातुं नेच्छसि, तथाप्य् अस्मद्-अभिप्रायानुसारेण तत् संपादय, इत्य् आह---नैतद् इति । हे अधीश ! नोऽस्माकं भजतां भूत-सूक्ष्म-रूपं पदं शब्दादि-विषय-सुखं मायया तनुषे विस्तारयसीति । यद् एतत् तव यद्य् अपि ईप्सितं न भवति, तथाप्य् अस्मद्-अनुग्रहायास् तु, ऋण-त्रयापाकरणानन्तरम् एवापवर्गाय भवत्व् इत्य् अर्थः । यर्हि यतो मायया परिच्छिन्न इव लसन्त्या तुलस्या युक्तस् त्वं विलक्षितोऽसि । एवं-भूतस्य तव दर्शनं यतो भुक्ति-मुक्ति-प्रदम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२०॥
word_for_word: yady api māyikatvād bhaktebhyo viṣaya-sukhaṃ dātuṃ necchasi tathāpy asmad-abhiprāyānusāreṇa tat saṃpādaya ity āha---naitad iti
although, because it is māyic, You may not wish to give sense-pleasure to Your devotees, nevertheless fulfill it in accordance with our intention
he adhīśa no’smākaṃ bhajatāṃ bhūta-sūkṣma-rūpaṃ padaṃ śabdādi-viṣaya-sukhaṃ māyayā tanuṣe vistārayasīti
“O Lord, You expand for us, Your worshipers, through māyā, the subtle-element state that is the basis of sense pleasures such as sound”
yad etat tava yady api īpsitaṃ na bhavati tathāpy asmad-anugrahāyās tu
although this may not be what You desire, let it be for Your favor to us
ṛṇa-trayāpākaraṇānantaram evāpavargāya bhavatv ity arthaḥ
after the three debts have been discharged, may it lead to liberation
yarhi yato māyayā paricchinna iva lasantyā tulasyā yuktas tvaṃ vilakṣito’si
since You are seen joined with Tulasī, shining as though bounded by māyā
evaṃ-bhūtasya tava darśanaṃ yato bhukti-mukti-pradam ity arthaḥ

entries.literal_english: “Although, because it is māyic, You may not wish to give sense-pleasure to Your devotees, nevertheless fulfill it in accordance with our intention,” he says with “naitad.” “O Lord, You do not expand for us, Your worshipers, through māyā the subtle-element state that is the basis of sense pleasures such as sound.” Although this may not be what You desire, let it be for Your favor to us; after the three debts have been discharged, may it lead to liberation. Since You are seen, joined with Tulasī, shining as though bounded by māyā, this vision of You grants both enjoyment and liberation.

entries.sanskrit: तं त्वा त्वां भुक्ति-मुक्ति-प्रदं नमामि । मुक्ति-दत्वे हेतुः, अनुभूत्या ज्ञानेनोपरतः क्रियार्थः कर्म-फल-भोगो यस्मिन् । भोग-दत्वे हेतुः, स्व-मायया आवर्तितं लोक-तन्त्रं विश्वोपकरणं येन । अतः स-कामैर् निष्कामैश् च नमनीयं पाद-सरोजं यस्य तम् । तत्राल्पीयसि स-कामे पुंसि भजने वा कामान् वर्षतीति तथा तम् ॥२१॥

bhoga-datve hetuḥ sva-māyayā āvartitaṃ loka-tantraṃ viśvopakaraṇaṃ yena

ataḥ sa-kāmair niṣkāmaiś ca namanīyaṃ pāda-sarojaṃ yasya tam
therefore Your lotus feet are to be bowed to by those with desires and by those without them
tatrālpīyasi sa-kāme puṃsi bhajane vā kāmān varṣatīti tathā tam
for one with only a small desire, or in a modest act of worship, You rain down the desired objects
entries.literal_english: I bow to You, who bestow both enjoyment and liberation. As the giver of liberation, You are the one in whom action directed toward its fruit is brought to rest through knowledge born of experience. As the giver of enjoyment, by Your own māyā You set in motion the order of the world, the instrument of the universe. Therefore Your lotus feet are to be bowed to by those with desires and by those without them. For a person with only a small desire, or in a modest act of worship, You are one who rains down the desired objects.

entries.sanskrit: गार्हस्थ्येन दयां कृत्वा, सन्न्यासेन अभयं दत्त्वा, मय्य् आत्मानं जगच् च सह एकीभूतं द्रक्ष्यसि ॥३१॥
word_for_word: gārhasthyena dayāṃ kṛtvā
by showing compassion through household life
sannyāsena abhayaṃ dattvā
by giving fearlessness through renunciation
mayy ātmānaṃ jagac ca saha ekībhūtaṃ drakṣyasi
you will see yourself and the world united as one in Me
entries.literal_english: By showing compassion through household life, and by giving fearlessness through renunciation, you will see yourself and the world united as one in Me.

entries.sanskrit: त्वद्-वीर्येण सह देवहूत्याम् अवतीर्येति शेषः ॥३२॥
word_for_word: tvad-vīryeṇa saha devahūtyām avatīryeti śeṣaḥ
it is understood that [Kapila] descended in Devahūti together with your potency
entries.literal_english: It is understood that [Kapila] descended in Devahūti together with your potency.

entries.sanskrit: प्रत्यग्-भूतेष्व् अक्षेषु जायते आविर्भवतीति प्रत्यग्-अक्षजः । सरस्वत्या नद्या परिश्रितात् परिवेष्टितात् ॥३३॥
word_for_word: pratyag-bhūteṣv akṣeṣu jāyate āvirbhavatīti pratyag-akṣajaḥ
“pratyag-akṣajaḥ” means that which is born or manifests in the inward senses
sarasvatyā nadyā pariśritāt pariveṣṭitāt
“pariśritāt” means surrounded by the river Sarasvatī
entries.literal_english: “Pratyag-akṣajaḥ” means that which is born or manifests in the inward senses. “Pariśritāt” means surrounded by the river Sarasvatī.

entries.sanskrit: अशेषैस् तपो-मन्त्रादि-सिद्धेश्वरैर् अभिष्टुतः सिद्ध-मार्गो वैकुण्ठ-मार्गो यस्य । यद् वा, अशेष-सिद्धेश्वराभिष्टुतश् चासौ सिद्धैर् मृग्यत इति सिद्ध-मार्गश् च स ययौ । पत्र-रथेन्द्रो गरुडस् तस्य पक्षैर् उदीर्णम् अभिव्यक्तं साम आकर्णयन्, बृहद्-रथान्तरे पक्षौ इति श्रुतेः । उच्चारितं स्तोमं च सामाधार-भूताणाम् ऋचां समुदायं शृण्वन् । स्तोम आत्मा इति श्रुतेः । समास-पाठे उच्चारितः स्तोमः स्तोत्रीय-समुदायो यस्य साम्न इति ॥३४॥
word_for_word: aśeṣais tapo-mantrādi-siddheśvarair abhiṣṭutaḥ
praised by all accomplished masters of austerity, mantra, and the rest
siddha-mārgo vaikuṇṭha-mārgo yasya
whose perfected path is the road to Vaikuṇṭha
yad vā aśeṣa-siddheśvarābhiṣṭutaś cāsau siddhair mṛgyata iti siddha-mārgaś ca sa yayau
or, praised by all accomplished lords, he went along the perfected path sought by the siddhas
patra-rathendro garuḍas tasya pakṣair udīrṇam abhivyaktaṃ sāma ākarṇayan
while listening to the Sāman song made manifest by the wings of Garuḍa, king of birds
bṛhad-rathāntare pakṣau iti śruteḥ
since the Śruti says that the Bṛhat and Rathantara Sāmans are his wings
uccāritaṃ stomaṃ ca sāmādhāra-bhūtāṇām ṛcāṃ samudāyaṃ śṛṇvan
and hearing the pronounced stoma, the collection of Ṛks that form the basis of the Sāmans
stoma ātmā iti śruteḥ
because the Śruti says, “the stoma is the self”
samāsa-pāṭhe uccāritaḥ stomaḥ stotrīya-samudāyo yasya sāmna iti
in the compound recitation, “pronounced stoma” means the collection of stotṛ verses belonging to the Sāman
entries.literal_english: His path is praised by all accomplished masters of austerity, mantra, and the rest: the perfected path is the road to Vaikuṇṭha. Or, he himself is praised by all accomplished lords, and he went along the perfected path sought by the siddhas. While listening to the Sāman song made manifest by the wings of Garuḍa, king of birds—since the Śruti says that the Bṛhat and Rathantara Sāmans are his wings—and hearing the pronounced stoma, the collection of Ṛks that form the basis of the Sāmans. The Śruti says, “the stoma is the self.” In the compound recitation, “pronounced stoma” means the collection of stotṛ verses belonging to the Sāman.

entries.sanskrit: तं कालं परश्व इत्य् उक्तं प्रतीक्षमाणः ॥३५॥
word_for_word: taṃ kālaṃ paraśva ity uktaṃ pratīkṣamāṇaḥ
awaiting that time, which is called “the day after tomorrow”
entries.literal_english: “Awaiting that time,” means waiting for the day called “the day after tomorrow.”

entries.sanskrit: शातकौम्भाः सौवर्णाः परिकरा यस्मिंस् तं रथम् आस्थाय, दुहितरं च आरोप्य, वरान्वेषणार्थं पर्यटन् ॥३६॥ हे सुधन्वन् विदुर । यद् अहः ॥३७॥
word_for_word: śātakaumbhāḥ sauvarṇāḥ parikarā yasmiṃs taṃ ratham āsthāya duhitaraṃ ca āropya varānveṣaṇārthaṃ paryaṭan
having mounted the chariot furnished with golden ornaments and seated his daughter in it, he traveled about in search of a bridegroom
he sudhanvan vidura
“O Sudhanvan” is an address to Vidura
yad ahaḥ
“on that day”
entries.literal_english: Having mounted the chariot furnished with golden ornaments and seated his daughter in it, he traveled about in search of a bridegroom. “O Sudhanvan” is an address to Vidura. “Yad ahaḥ” means “on that day.”

entries.sanskrit: तत् प्रवेश-मात्रेण परमानन्दं प्राप्त इति दर्शयितुम् आश्रमं वर्णयति---यस्मिन्न् इत्य्-आदिभिः सप्तभिः श्लोकैः । प्रपन्ने कर्दमे ॥३८॥ शिवम् आरोग्यम् अमृतवत् स्वादु जलं यस्मिन् ॥३९॥
word_for_word: tat praveśa-mātreṇa paramānandaṃ prāpta iti darśayitum āśramaṃ varṇayati---yasminn ity-ādibhiḥ saptabhiḥ ślokaiḥ
to show that he attained supreme bliss simply upon entering, the hermitage is described in seven verses beginning with “yasmin”
prapanne kardame
when Kardama received him
śivam ārogyam
“śivam” means health
amṛtavat svādu jalaṃ yasmin
the water there is tasty like nectar
entries.literal_english: To show that he attained supreme bliss simply upon entering, the hermitage is described in seven verses beginning with “yasmin,” when Kardama received him. “Śivam” means health; the water there is tasty like nectar.

entries.sanskrit: कूजन्तः पुण्या मृगा द्विजाश् च येषु, तैः पुण्य-द्रुम-लतानां जालैः समूहैर् युक्तम् ॥४०॥
word_for_word: kūjantaḥ puṇyā mṛgā dvijāś ca yeṣu
in which are sacred deer and birds that call out
taiḥ puṇya-druma-latānāṃ jālaiḥ samūhair yuktam
it is furnished with clusters of auspicious trees and vines
entries.literal_english: It is furnished with clusters of auspicious trees and vines, and with sacred deer and birds that call out.

entries.sanskrit: घुष्टं नादितम् । मत्त-भ्रमराणां विभ्रमो विनोदो यस्मिन् । मत्ता बर्हिण एव नटास् तेषाम् आटोपो नृत्य-संभ्रमो यस्मिन् । आह्वयन्तो मिथो मत्ताः कोकिला यस्मिन् ॥४१॥
word_for_word: ghuṣṭaṃ nāditam
“ghuṣṭam” means resounding
matta-bhramarāṇāṃ vibhramo vinodo yasmin
where the intoxicated bees sport
mattā barhiṇa eva naṭās teṣām āṭopo nṛtya-saṃbhramo yasmin
where the intoxicated peacocks are dancers, their movement a display of dancing
āhvayanto mitho mattāḥ kokilā yasmin
where the excited cuckoos call to one another
entries.literal_english: “Ghuṣṭam” means resounding. There the intoxicated bees sport; the intoxicated peacocks are dancers, their movement a display of dancing; and the excited cuckoos call to one another.

entries.sanskrit: कदम्बादिभिर् वृक्षैर् अलङ्कृतम् ॥४२॥
word_for_word: kadambādibhir vṛkṣair alaṅkṛtam
adorned with trees such as the kadamba
entries.literal_english: It is adorned with trees such as the kadamba.

entries.sanskrit: कारणडवादिभिः पक्षिभिर् वल्गु यथा तथा कूजितम् ॥४३॥
word_for_word: kāraṇaḍavādibhiḥ pakṣibhir valgu yathā tathā kūjitam
the birds called kāraṇḍava and the others coo sweetly
entries.literal_english: The birds called kāraṇḍava and the others coo sweetly.

entries.sanskrit: हरिणादिभिर् वृतम् । तत्र क्रोडः सूकरः । श्वाविच् छल्लकः । मर्को मर्कटः । तद्-विशेषो गो-पुच्छः । हरिर् वानरः सिंहो व । नाभिः कस्तूरी-मृगः ॥४४॥
word_for_word: hariṇādibhir vṛtam
surrounded by deer and other animals
tatra kroḍaḥ sūkaraḥ
there “kroḍa” means boar
śvāvic challakaḥ
“śvāvid” means porcupine
marko markaṭaḥ
“marka” means monkey
tad-viśeṣo go-pucchaḥ
a particular kind is the gopuccha
harir vānaraḥ siṃho va
“hari” means monkey or lion
nābhiḥ kastūrī-mṛgaḥ
“nābhi” means musk deer
entries.literal_english: The place is surrounded by deer and other animals. Here “kroḍa” means boar, “śvāvid” means porcupine, “marka” means monkey, and a particular kind is the gopuccha. “Hari” means either monkey or lion; “nābhi” means musk deer.

entries.sanskrit: हुतो हुताशनो ब्रह्मचारि-योग्यो येन ॥४५॥
word_for_word: huto hutāśano brahmacāri-yogyo yena
in it the sacred fire was offered, suitable for a celibate student and for ascetics
entries.literal_english: In it the sacred fire was offered, suitable for a celibate student and for ascetics.

entries.sanskrit: उग्रा युक् योगो यस्य तेन वपुषा विद्योतमानम् । तस्य भगवतो व्याहृतं भाषणम् एव अमृत-कला अमृत-मयस्य चन्द्रस्य कला तन्सयं पीयूषं तस्य श्रवणेन च नातिक्षामं तपसा कृशं सन्तम् अप्य् अकृशम् ॥४६॥
word_for_word: ugrā yuk yogo yasya tena vapuṣā vidyotamānam
shining with a body whose discipline was intense
tasya bhagavato vyāhṛtaṃ bhāṣaṇam eva amṛta-kalā amṛta-mayasya candrasya kalā tan-sayaṃ pīyūṣaṃ
the speech of the Lord Himself was a drop of nectar, a digit of the nectar-filled moon
tasya śravaṇena ca nātikṣāmaṃ tapasā kṛśaṃ santam apy akṛśam
by hearing it he was not excessively emaciated—though wasted by austerity, he was not wasted
entries.literal_english: He was shining with a body whose discipline was intense. The speech of the Lord Himself was a drop of nectar, a digit of the nectar-filled moon; by hearing it he was not excessively emaciated—though wasted by austerity, he was not wasted.

entries.sanskrit: प्रांशुम् उन्नतम् । उपसंसृत्य समीपं गत्वा मलिनं ददर्शेति पूर्वैव क्रिया । अर्ह्यतेऽनेनेत्य् अर्हणं महा-रत्नं तद् असंस्कृतम् अनिर्णिक्तं यथा मलिनं दृश्यते तद्वत् ॥४७॥
word_for_word: prāṃśum unnatam
“prāṃśum” means tall, elevated
upasaṃsṛtya samīpaṃ gatvā
“having approached” means having gone near
malinaṃ dadarśeti pūrvaiva kriyā
“he saw the soiled one” is connected with the preceding action
arhyate’nenety arhaṇaṃ mahā-ratnaṃ
“arhaṇa” is a great jewel used for worship
tad asaṃskṛtam anirṇiktaṃ yathā malinaṃ dṛśyate tadvat
unworked and unpolished, it appears dirty
entries.literal_english: “Prāṃśum” means tall, elevated. “Having approached” means having gone near. “He saw the soiled one” is connected with the preceding action. “Arhaṇa” is a great jewel used for worship; unworked and unpolished, it appears dirty.

entries.sanskrit: उटजं पर्ण-शालां प्रप्तं । पुरः पाद-समीपे प्रणतम् आशीर्भिर् अभिनन्द्य सपर्यया पूजया प्रत्यगृह्णात् सत्-कृतवान् ॥४८॥
word_for_word: uṭajaṃ parṇa-śālāṃ praptaṃ
“uṭajam” means a leaf hut; he had arrived there
puraḥ pāda-samīpe praṇatam
bowed before him, near his feet
āśīrbhir abhinandya saparyayā pūjayā pratyagṛhṇāt sat-kṛtavān
having welcomed him with blessings, Kardama received and honored him with worship
entries.literal_english: “Uṭajam” means a leaf hut; he had arrived there. Having welcomed him with blessings while he bowed at his feet, Kardama received and honored him with worship.

“te” means his pacing about, his wandering
hi yasmāt
“hi” means “because”
entries.literal_english: “Te” means his pacing about, his wandering. “Hi” means “because.”

entries.sanskrit: मनु-स्थं विष्णुं प्रणमति---य इति । स्थाने तत्-तत्-कार्यावसरे शुक्लाय विष्णवे ॥५१॥

he bows to Viṣṇu situated in Manu, saying “yaḥ”
sthāne tat-tat-kāryāvasare
“sthāne” means at the proper place, at the occasion for each particular task
śuklāya viṣṇave
to Śukla, Viṣṇu
entries.literal_english: He bows to Viṣṇu situated in Manu, saying “yaḥ.” “Sthāne” means at the proper place, at the occasion for each particular task; [he bows] to Śukla, Viṣṇu.

entries.sanskrit: न यदेति पञ्चानाम् अयम् अर्थः---यद्यपि धर्म-रक्षार्थं सर्वतः पर्यटतस् तव प्रसङ्गाद् अप्य् आगमनं संभवति तथापि विशेष-कार्यं चेद् अस्ति तत् कथ्यताम् इति । जैत्रं जय-प्रदं मणि-गणा अर्पिता यस्मिंस् तं रथम् आरुह्य त्वं यदा भुवो मण्डलं न पर्यटसि तदा सेतवो भिद्येरन्न् इति त्रयाणाम् अन्वयः । विस्फूर्जन्-नादं कुर्व-चण्डं कोदण्डं धनुर् यस्य । वर्णाश्रमाणां निबन्धनं यैः । बत अहो ॥५२-५४॥
word_for_word: na yadeti pañcānām ayam arthaḥ
this is the meaning of the five verses beginning “na yadet”
yadyapi dharma-rakṣārthaṃ sarvataḥ paryaṭatas tava prasaṅgād apy āgamanaṃ saṃbhavati tathāpi viśeṣa-kāryaṃ ced asti tat kathyatām iti
although Your coming may be occasioned by Your roaming everywhere to protect dharma, nevertheless, if there is a special task, please state it
jaitraṃ jaya-pradaṃ maṇi-gaṇā arpitā yasmiṃs taṃ ratham āruhya tvaṃ yadā bhuvo maṇḍalaṃ na paryaṭasi tadā setavo bhidyerann iti trayāṇām anvayaḥ
“jaitra” means victory-giving; the chariot is adorned with a row of gems. The syntax is: “When You do not travel around the circle of the earth mounted on that chariot, the bridges would break”
visphūrjan-nādaṃ kurva-caṇḍaṃ kodaṇḍaṃ dhanur yasya
He whose bow makes a fierce, resounding sound
varṇāśramāṇāṃ nibandhanaṃ yaiḥ
“those by whom the social and spiritual orders are established”
bata aho
“bata” means “ah!”
entries.literal_english: This is the meaning of the five verses beginning “na yadet”: “Although Your coming may be occasioned by Your roaming everywhere to protect dharma, nevertheless, if there is a special task, please state it.” “Jaitra” means victory-giving; the chariot is adorned with a row of gems. The syntax of three verses is: “When You do not travel around the circle of the earth mounted on that chariot, the bridges would break.” He whose bow makes a fierce, resounding sound; “those by whom the social and spiritual orders are established”; “bata” means “ah!”
